identity.title: A Virus-like particle system based on parainfluenza virus PIV5-L for CRISPR-Cas9 and RNAi delivery.

content.abstract: Nucleic acid-targeting technologies based on CRISPR-Cas or small-hairpin RNA (shRNA) are essential for functional genomics and therapeutic development, yet a delivery platform that simultaneously ensures high efficiency, safety, modularity, and broad cell compatibility remains lacking. Here, we report L-VLP, a virus-like particle platform derived from a B-lymphoma-isolated strain of parainfluenza virus PIV5-L. This single-cycle, replication-deficient VLP functions as a dual-mode delivery system, capable of carrying either Cas9/sgRNA for CRISPR-mediated gene editing or shRNA for RNA interference, and achieves effective target gene knockdown or knockout in both breast cancer and B-lymphoma cells. Notably, the sgRNA or shRNA cassettes in L-VLP can be readily exchanged for any sequence of interest without altering the core vector architecture, providing a modular and versatile design. Functional assays confirm that L-VLP-mediated UBR5 silencing significantly inhibits tumor cell growth in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our work establishes L-VLP as a flexible and efficient platform for manipulating gene expression, with promising applications in both basic research and cancer target therapeutics.
